title: Challenge: Changing Casing in Text
summary: Introduces toUpperCase() and toLowerCase() for changing the case of a string, shows that the result must be reassigned to persist, then sets a challenge: prompt for a name and alert a greeting where only the first letter is capitalised.

concepts.heading: toUpperCase() and toLowerCase()
points: Both are string methods called with dot notation on a variable: name.toUpperCase() returns the string with every character in capitals; name.toLowerCase() returns it in small letters.
The parentheses are required even though no argument is passed, and the statement ends with a semicolon.
In the console demo the uppercase string is printed, but checking name afterwards still shows the original lowercase text.
(Extra) Strings are immutable in JavaScript, so these methods never edit the original; they return a new string.

concepts.heading: Keeping the changed value
points: To keep the result, reassign it to the same variable: name = name.toUpperCase();
Reassigning with name = name.toLowerCase(); later lowercases the whole value, including the first letter that had been capitalised.
Typing the variable name in the console after running shows its current value, which is a quick way to verify a reassignment worked.

concepts.heading: Why casing matters
points: Users type input inconsistently (all lowercase, all caps, mixed). Normalising case before printing makes output such as an alert look consistent across users.

code_examples.caption: Changing case and reassigning
code_examples.code:
var name = "Angela";
name.toUpperCase();          // returns "ANGELA" but name is unchanged
name = name.toUpperCase();   // now name holds "ANGELA"
name = name.toLowerCase();   // now name holds "angela"

task.name: Capitalise the first letter of a name
task.starting_point: Empty script in the editor (reference repo: index.html linking script.js).
task.goal: Ask the user for their name with a prompt and show an alert greeting them, with only the first character capitalised and the rest lowercase, regardless of how it was typed.
steps: Use prompt() to ask for the name and store it in a variable.
Slice out the first character with slice(0, 1).
Slice out the remainder from index 1 to the end.
Uppercase the first part and lowercase the remainder.
Concatenate a greeting, the capitalised letter and the remainder, then pass it to alert().
Constraint: use only techniques from this module (slice, concatenation, case methods), not Stack Overflow shortcuts.
task.expected_result: Entering aNGELA, ANGELA or angela all produce an alert reading Hello Angela.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 14 - Introduction to Javascript ES6/14.08 - Challenge - Changing Casing in Text

pitfalls: Calling name.toUpperCase() without assigning the result leaves the variable unchanged.
Forgetting the parentheses turns the call into a reference to the method rather than running it.
Reference repo page has an author footer; ignore it.

playground.coverage: Covers the same challenge with four tasks, a starter, a solution that also shows chaining, and notes on both methods and immutability.
gaps_and_ideas: Add a task that demonstrates the reassignment gotcha (call toUpperCase without assigning, log the variable, then fix it).
Add a live input box in the explore demo showing the original and normalised strings side by side.
Mention that an empty prompt or Cancel (null) will make name.slice fail, as a stretch task.
